name: Culver V
summary: Postwar two-seat cabin low-wing built by Culver, known for its Simpli-Fly one-knob flap/trim control. Retractable tricycle gear and a distinctive upward-bent outer wing.

wings: Low cantilever wing with outer panels angled sharply upward (pronounced dihedral break)
engines: Single Continental flat-four (85-95 hp) in a smooth cowl
fuselage: Enclosed side-by-side two-seat cabin with a rounded glasshouse

tellTales: Low wing whose outer panels angle upward
Two-seat cabin on retractable tricycle gear
No struts and a clean, rounded cabin

confusedWith.howToTell: The Cadet is a prewar tailwheel two-seater with a conventional wing; the V has tricycle gear and a pronounced upward bend in the outer wing.
The Ercoupe has twin fins; the Culver V has a single fin and retractable gear.
The Mite is a tiny single-seater; the Culver V is a two-seater with a larger cabin.
